messages:
Jordan: Heads-up — hit a weird warmup failure for sharded safetensors when serving from S3.
Jordan: Repro steps: we upload shards (gzipped) and a manifest.json.gz that lists byte offsets for each shard assuming uncompressed layout.
Jordan: During warmup we do ranged GETs against the gzipped shard objects using the manifest offsets and the integrity hashes fail.
Jordan: Hypothesis: S3 range semantics operate on the compressed bytes, but manifest offsets were computed on uncompressed lengths (we gzipped offline after packing). So ranges don't line up.
Maya: Yep saw this in a canary yesterday. S3+Content-Encoding gzip means byte ranges refer to stored (compressed) payload. If manifest offsets are post-decompression, ranges return wrong slices.
Maya: Two quick fixes: 1) keep manifest uncompressed and authoritative for compressed offsets or 2) ensure packing step computes offsets on the compressed payload and writes compressed_offset/compressed_length per shard.
Ian: I think long-term we need manifest v2 that explicitly declares mode: "compression-aware" with fields: compressed_offset, compressed_length, uncompressed_length, compression: "gzip".
Ian: Fallback behaviour during warmup: try compressed-range streaming if compressed_offset present; else fall back to full-object fetch for that shard (or manifestless stream + verify hash).
Jordan: Can we avoid full-object fetches? warmup time matters.
Maya: We can optimize: do a small head_object to get Content-Length and ETag, then only fetch the minimal compressed range. But if offsets are wrong we'll detect hash mismatch and then fetch the full shard.
Ian: Also consider using multipart ETags — they break simple etag-based validation. Add part_etags in manifest if we rely on multipart uploads for large shards.
WeightsBot: Quick verification snippet that helped me:
WeightsBot: ```python
WeightsBot: import boto3, hashlib
WeightsBot: s3 = boto3.client('s3')
WeightsBot: r = s3.get_object(Bucket='redwood-weights', Key='shard-000.gz', Range='bytes=1000-1999')
WeightsBot: chunk = r['Body'].read()
WeightsBot: print('len', len(chunk))
WeightsBot: # compute hash against expected compressed hash if available
WeightsBot: print(hashlib.sha256(chunk).hexdigest())
WeightsBot: ```
OpsBot: CI note: added an integration test to infra/warmup that uploads gzipped shard+manifest with mismatched offsets and expects graceful fallback (PR queued).
Maya: Operational policy idea: when publishing model bundles to our blobstore, include both manifest.json (uncompressed, compressed offsets) and manifest.json.gz for convenience. That avoids accidental recompute ordering bugs.
Ian: Action items: @Maya update bundler to emit manifest v2 (compressed offsets + part_etags) — target next sprint. @Jordan add warmup fallback logic: try compressed-range if offsets present, else manifestless stream then full fetch. @OpsBot keep the test in CI.
Jordan: SGTM. I'll file a short RFC draft for manifest v2 and link the CI failure logs. Thanks all :thumbsup:
